2027-06-27.title: Seventh Sunday of the Apostles
2027-06-27.readTitle: Readings of the day (First Set; mapped from the official calendar, verify locally)
readings: You heard the sound of words but saw no form
The Holy God shows himself holy by righteousness
Let all that you do be done in love
Strive to enter through the narrow door
2027-06-27.alt: Season of the Apostles (Šleehe), which began at Pentecost: the Church remembers how the apostles, filled with the Holy Spirit, carried the Gospel to the nations. The Holy Qurbana is celebrated with the Anaphora of Addai and Mari, and from Pentecost the Angel of the Lord (Angelus) is prayed again in place of the Queen of Heaven. Today is the last Sunday of the Season of the Apostles. The calendar gives longer forms: Deuteronomy 4:10–24; Isaiah 5:8–25; 1 Corinthians 15:58–16:24; Luke 13:22–35. Looking ahead: the Dukhrana of St Thomas on Saturday 3 July, and the Season of Kaitha (Qaita) from Sunday 4 July. In the Latin calendar today is the Thirteenth Sunday in Ordinary Time.
2027-06-27.verse: Strive to enter through the narrow door; for many, I tell you, will try to enter and will not be able.
theo: The Season of the Apostles ends today as it began, with a word heard from the fire. At Pentecost the Spirit came on the apostles in tongues of fire; in the first reading Moses reminds Israel of the day they stood at Horeb “while the mountain was blazing up to the very heavens, shrouded in dark clouds.” God had said to Moses, “Assemble the people for me, and I will let them hear my words, so that they may learn to fear me as long as they live on the earth, and may teach their children so.” Then the decisive line: “Then the Lord spoke to you out of the fire. You heard the sound of words but saw no form; there was only a voice.” Israel's God is not a statue that can be carried or bought; he is a living God who speaks and makes a covenant, written on two tablets of stone. Faith comes by hearing, and it lives by being taught to children. In Kerala this month the schools have reopened, and in our parishes the faith formation classes have begun again on Sunday mornings. Moses would call that holy work. The voice without form has now taken a face: “No one has ever seen God. It is God the only Son, who is close to the Father’s heart, who has made him known” (John 1:18). The apostles heard that voice, saw that face and handed both on to us.

Isaiah's reading follows the Song of the Vineyard, in which God looked for justice in his people and found bloodshed, looked for righteousness and heard a cry (Isaiah 5:7). Now come the woes. “Ah, you who join house to house, who add field to field, until there is room for no one but you, and you are left to live alone in the midst of the land!” Greed that swallows the land of the poor ends in loneliness: large and beautiful houses “without inhabitant”. Many Kerala villages know the sight of great locked houses whose owners live abroad and whose aged parents are alone. Then: “Ah, you who rise early in the morning in pursuit of strong drink, who linger in the evening to be inflamed by wine,” with music at every feast, “but who do not regard the deeds of the Lord.” Our State knows the cost of that woe in broken families and early deaths. And the deepest woe: “Ah, you who call evil good and good evil, who put darkness for light and light for darkness.” When a society renames sin as progress and calls goodness foolish, it has lost its way. Yet in the middle of the woes stands the Holy One: “the Lord of hosts is exalted by justice, and the Holy God shows himself holy by righteousness.” God is not defeated by our confusion; his holiness will shine in justice.

Paul's letter closes with practical matters, and they show us the apostolic Church at work. “Now concerning the collection for the saints”: the churches founded among the Gentiles were gathering money for the poor of the mother Church in Jerusalem. “On the first day of every week, each of you is to put aside and save whatever extra you earn.” Here, in one of the earliest Christian writings, the first day of the week, the day of the Resurrection, is already the day of giving, just as Acts tells us it was the day “when we met to break bread” (Acts 20:7). Paul then shares his plans: “I will stay in Ephesus until Pentecost, for a wide door for effective work has opened to me, and there are many adversaries.” An open door and many adversaries: that is the life of every apostle. He commends young Timothy, “let no one despise him”, and speaks warmly of Apollos. And he gives five commands that could sum up the whole Season of the Apostles: “Keep alert, stand firm in your faith, be courageous, be strong. Let all that you do be done in love.” Our Sunday offering, our help to the mission dioceses of North India and to the poor of our own parish, belongs to this same apostolic love.

In the Gospel Jesus is on the road to Jerusalem, and someone asks the question people still ask: “Lord, will only a few be saved?” Jesus does not answer with a number. He turns curiosity into a call: “Strive to enter through the narrow door.” The word for strive is the word for an athlete's struggle; salvation is a gift, but it is received by those who make the effort of conversion. Then a hard picture: the owner of the house has shut the door, and those outside knock: “Lord, open to us.” “We ate and drank with you, and you taught in our streets.” They had been near Jesus, had shared meals with him and heard him preach, yet he says, “I do not know where you come from.” Nearness without conversion is not enough. Baptism, a Christian name, a seat in church on feast days: these are graces, but they do not replace a life turned to God. And then the door opens wide: “Then people will come from east and west, from north and south, and will eat in the kingdom of God.” The apostles carried this invitation to every direction of the earth, and Mar Thoma brought it to our shores. “Indeed, some are last who will be first, and some are first who will be last.” Those who came late may be first at the table. As the Season of the Apostles closes, the Church asks us: have we entered through the narrow door ourselves, and are we holding it open for those still outside?
conn: “No one has ever seen God. It is God the only Son, who is close to the Father’s heart, who has made him known” (John 1:18); “Whoever has seen me has seen the Father” (John 14:9).

“Keep these words that I am commanding you today in your heart. Recite them to your children and talk about them when you are at home and when you are away, when you lie down and when you rise” (Deuteronomy 6:6–7).

Isaiah's woes follow the Song of the Vineyard: “he expected justice, but saw bloodshed; righteousness, but heard a cry!” (Isaiah 5:7). Jesus takes up the vineyard in the parable of the wicked tenants (Matthew 21:33–43).
The first day of the week.

“On the first day of the week, when we met to break bread, Paul was holding a discussion with them” (Acts 20:7). The collection for Jerusalem: “Macedonia and Achaia have been pleased to share their resources with the poor among the saints at Jerusalem” (Romans 15:26).
“For the gate is narrow and the road is hard that leads to life, and there are few who find it” (Matthew 7:14); “I am the gate. Whoever enters by me will be saved” (John 10:9).
“For from the rising of the sun to its setting my name is great among the nations” (Malachi 1:11).
altar: The voice that Israel heard from the fire at Horeb speaks to us at every Holy Qurbana in the readings, and the One who has made the Father known gives himself to us in his Body and Blood. Here already people from east and west, north and south, sit at the table of the kingdom.

The first day of the week is the day of the Qurbana and the day of giving. The bread and wine we offer, and the offering we place in the box, are one act of love: the Lord receives both and sends us out to let all that we do be done in love.
outline: The last Sunday of the Season of the Apostles: from the fire of Horeb and Pentecost to the table of the kingdom.
God speaks and makes a covenant; faith is heard and taught to children.
Point 2 · The woes of the vineyard
Greed for land, strong drink, and calling evil good; the Holy God shows himself holy by righteousness.
Point 3 · Let all be done in love
The collection on the first day of the week; a wide door and many adversaries.
Not how many, but am I entering? East and west at the table.
A small tin box beside the family altar, filled each Sunday.
“Strive to enter through the narrow door.”
live: Parents: sit with your children for ten minutes this week and ask what they learned in the faith formation class; pray together afterwards.
Name one place where you have called evil good, or where drink or greed has a hold in your home, and take one step to change it.
Give on the first day (1 Corinthians 16:2)
Set aside a fixed amount every Sunday this coming season for the poor or the missions, before any other spending.
Choose one concrete effort of conversion for the week: confession, reconciliation with someone, or a daily time of prayer.
fathers: How far, you rich, will you stretch your mad greed? Will you alone live on the earth? Why do you drive out the one who shares your nature and claim the creation for yourself? The earth was made for all in common, rich and poor alike. When you give to the poor, you do not give from what is yours; you return what is his.

Paul says, on the first day of the week let each put something aside. Let us do the same: let there be a little box for the poor in your house, beside the place where you stand to pray. Each time you pray, put something in it. Then your house will be a church, and the money of the poor will guard your house better than any weapon.

The Lord did not answer the question of how many are saved, because it was of no use to the hearer. He showed the way instead. The narrow door is the life of virtue, which is entered with effort; but those who have entered find it opens on a wide and joyful dwelling with Christ.
magis: The affirmations of Sacred Scripture and the teachings of the Church on hell are a call to responsibility: Enter by the narrow gate, for the gate is wide and the way is easy that leads to destruction.
The practice of the Christian assembly on the Lord's Day dates from the beginnings of the apostolic age; the Letter to the Hebrews reminds the faithful not to neglect to meet together.
Education in the faith by the parents should begin in the child's earliest years; parents have the mission of teaching their children to pray and to discover their vocation as children of God.
The virtue of temperance disposes us to avoid every kind of excess: the abuse of food, alcohol, tobacco or medicine.
The right to private property does not do away with the original gift of the earth to the whole of mankind; the universal destination of goods remains primordial.
saints: Seventh Sunday of the Apostles, the last Sunday of the season. In the Latin calendar, the Thirteenth Sunday in Ordinary Time.
Mon 28: St Irenaeus. Tue 29: St Peter and St Paul, the Apostles, an important feast and a day of obligation. Sat 3 July: the Dukhrana of St Thomas. Sun 4 July: the Season of Kaitha begins.
2027-06-27.prayer: Lord God, you spoke to your people out of the fire at Horeb, and at Pentecost you sent the fire of your Spirit on the apostles. Through this season you have taught us the faith they handed on: keep it alive in our homes, and help us to teach it to our children. Deliver us from greed, from strong drink and from calling evil good; show yourself holy among us by righteousness. Make us generous on the first day of every week, alert, firm in faith, courageous and strong, and let all that we do be done in love. Lord Jesus, you are the narrow door: give us strength to enter, and gather people from east and west, north and south, to your table in the kingdom. Glory to the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit, for ever. Amen.

quick: Deuteronomy: at Horeb you heard the sound of words but saw no form; learn to fear the Lord and teach your children.
Isaiah: woe to those who join field to field, who chase strong drink, who call evil good; the Holy God shows himself holy by righteousness.

2027-06-27.action: Set up a small box for the poor beside your family altar and put something in it every Sunday.
2027-06-27.question: Am I striving to enter the narrow door, or only standing near it?
catechism: The Lord's Day from apostolic times.
kidsaint: Father Chavara was a priest in Kerala about two hundred years ago. He loved God and he loved children. He started a school at Mannanam and asked that every parish should have a school beside the church, so that all children, rich or poor, could learn to read and write and learn about Jesus. He also began a religious congregation of priests and one of sisters. Pope Francis declared him a saint in 2014. Lesson: when school begins, thank God for your teachers, and learn well for Jesus!
2027-06-27.special: Seventh Sunday of the Apostles, the last Sunday of the season. Kaitha begins on Sunday 4 July.
term: The East Syriac liturgical season that follows the Season of the Apostles. Qaita means summer, the time of fruit: after the apostles have sown the Gospel, the Church contemplates its growth and fruit in the saints and martyrs. In 2027 it begins on Sunday 4 July, the day after the Dukhrana of St Thomas. Malayalam: കൈത്താക്കാലം.

family.explain: Someone asked Jesus: will only a few people be saved? Jesus said: try hard to go in through the narrow door. A narrow door means we cannot carry everything with us: we leave behind selfishness, lies and bad habits. But Jesus also said that people from east and west, north and south will come and sit at God's table. God wants everyone to come in!
family.intention: We pray for children starting a new school year, for their teachers, and for children who cannot go to school.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing our family needs to leave outside so that we can go in through the narrow door?”

illus: In a house near Pala (a story told to illustrate the reading) an old grandmother kept a small tin box beside the family altar, under the picture of the Sacred Heart. Every Sunday after the Holy Qurbana, she asked each grandchild to put in one coin from their own pocket money, and the adults put in what they could. Nobody opened the box during the year. In June, when the schools reopened, the grandmother called the family together and opened it, and they counted the money on the dining table. It was enough to pay the school fees, uniforms and books for a child in a poor family of the parish. The children were allowed to choose the colour of the umbrella for the monsoon. ‘Saint Paul told the Corinthians to put something aside on the first day of every week,’ the grandmother used to say. ‘The box is small, but love fills it.’ Years later, one of those grandchildren, now working abroad, still keeps a tin box beside his own family altar.

pm.open: Holy Spirit, who spoke from the fire and came upon the apostles, gather us at the end of this Season of the Apostles. Keep us alert, firm and strong, and let all that we do be done in love. Amen.
share: You heard the sound of words but saw no form (Deuteronomy 4:12). How do I listen to God's word?
Ah, you who call evil good and good evil (Isaiah 5:20). Where have I renamed sin to make it comfortable?
Let all that you do be done in love (1 Corinthians 16:14). What do I do without love?
Strive to enter through the narrow door (Luke 13:24). What must I leave behind to enter?
pm.resp: Lord, open to us the door of your kingdom.
interc: For the Church at the close of the Season of the Apostles, that she may be alert, firm in faith and courageous in mission.
For children and teachers at the beginning of the school year, and for those who teach the faith in our parishes.
For families harmed by alcohol, greed and quarrels over land, that they may find healing and peace.
For the poor and the missions, that our Sunday giving may be generous.
For all peoples of east and west, north and south, that they may come to the table of the kingdom.
pm.close: Father, you spoke from the fire and made your face known in your Son. As this Season of the Apostles closes, keep us faithful to the faith they handed on, generous in love, and striving to enter the narrow door, until we sit at your table with all your saints. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, today is the last Sunday of the Season of the Apostles. It began at Pentecost with tongues of fire, and the first reading takes us back to another fire, at Mount Horeb. There God spoke to his people: “You heard the sound of words but saw no form; there was only a voice” (Deuteronomy 4:12). Our God is not a statue; he is a God who speaks.

Moses says that the people must learn this word and teach it to their children. This month the schools have reopened and the faith formation classes have begun again. Parents, you are the first teachers of the faith. Ask your children what they have learned, and pray with them.

Isaiah warns against three woes: greed that joins field to field until no one else has room, strong drink from morning to night, and calling evil good and good evil (Isaiah 5:8, 11, 20). Our families know all three. Let us ask the Holy God to make us holy by righteousness.

Saint Paul asks the Corinthians to put something aside on the first day of every week for the poor in Jerusalem. Already then, Sunday was the day of the breaking of bread and the day of giving. And he gives us five words for the road: “Keep alert, stand firm in your faith, be courageous, be strong. Let all that you do be done in love” (1 Corinthians 16:13–14).

In the Gospel someone asks, “Lord, will only a few be saved?” Jesus does not give a number. He says: “Strive to enter through the narrow door” (Luke 13:24). It is not enough to have eaten and drunk near him; we must turn our lives to him.

But the door is open to all: people will come from east and west, from north and south, and sit at the table of the kingdom. The apostles carried this invitation to the whole world, and Mar Thoma brought it to us. As this season closes, let us enter the narrow door ourselves and hold it open for others. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says: try hard to go in through the narrow door. To go through a narrow door you must leave your big bags outside! Leave outside lies, selfishness and bad words.
And Jesus says people will come from every side of the world to sit at God's table. God wants everyone in his house. This week, help a friend to come closer to Jesus!

On the last Sunday of the Season of the Apostles: the voice from the fire, the woes of the vineyard, the apostolic love that gives on the first day of the week, and the narrow door that opens on the feast of all nations.

concl: The Season of the Apostles closes with the voice of God, the call to justice, the love that gives and the door of the kingdom.
Let us enter the narrow door ourselves and hold it open for all peoples.
2027-06-27.resolve: This week, teach the faith at home, refuse one woe, set aside a Sunday gift for the poor, and make one real effort of conversion.
